description:
Profile refusals and divergences reach machine consumers as structured details and suggested
resolutions rather than as one flat sentence.

## Background

Two failure branches build their machine-readable output from the error's rendered text alone,
discarding the typed value behind it. The same output type already supports attached details
and suggestions, and two neighbouring profile subcommands already use it to carry structured
findings — so the pattern is proven on this exact surface and needs extending to the refusal
paths rather than inventing.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A refused profile publication emits its conflict code together with structured details naming each conflicting target, its conflict class, and its typed remedy.
- [hard] REQ-02: A reported divergence emits structured details naming each diverged target, its divergence class, and its typed remedy.
- [hard] REQ-03: Suggested resolutions accompany the details and name capture only where the remedy marks capture applicable.
- [hard] REQ-04: The failure code, the exit status, and the rendered human message of both paths keep their current content.
- [hard] REQ-05: Existing coverage reading these failures asserts the structured fields rather than the sentence alone.

## Notes

Coverage for this surface lives in the command-boundary suites, so the assertions run against
the process an adopter actually invokes.
title: Profile conflict output carries its remedy
